Bantha Stew

Served at: Life Day (Wookiee Tradition)

Serves 8Prep 30 minCook 2 hours

Bantha Stew is a cornerstone of the Life Day feast, a hearty and warming dish traditionally shared among Wookiee families on Kashyyyk. This rich, savory stew, often prepared over an open hearth, symbolizes the warmth of family bonds and the sustenance of life, making it perfect for celebrating the annual Wookiee holiday of peace and harmony.

Ingredients

  • 2 lbs (900g) Bantha steak or shoulder, cut into 1-inch (2.5 cm) cubes
  • 2 tablespoons Bantha butter or cooking oil
  • 2 large Nerf onions, chopped
  • 3 cloves Garrmorl garlic, minced
  • 4 medium Ryshcate roots (similar to potatoes), peeled and cubed
  • 2 large Corellian carrots, peeled and sliced
  • 1 cup (240ml) dry red wine (optional)
  • 4 cups (960ml) Bantha bone broth or beef broth
  • 1 (14.5 oz / 410g) can crushed Lothal tomatoes
  • 2 tablespoons spiceleaf blend (e.g., bay leaf, thyme, rosemary)
  • 1 teaspoon salt, or to taste
  • 1/2 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, or to taste
  • 1/2 cup (120g) Gribbet greens (like spinach or kale), roughly chopped
  • 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour
  • 1/4 cup (60ml) cold water

Method

  1. Pat the Bantha meat dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
  2. In a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, heat the Bantha butter or oil over medium-high heat. Brown the Bantha meat in batches on all sides until well-seared, then remove from the pot and set aside.
  3. Add the chopped Nerf onions to the pot and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced Garrmorl garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
  4. Pour in the red wine (if using) and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Let it simmer for 2-3 minutes until slightly reduced.
  5. Return the browned Bantha meat to the pot. Add the Ryshcate roots, Corellian carrots, Bantha bone broth, crushed Lothal tomatoes, and spiceleaf blend. Stir to combine.
  6. Bring the stew to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for at least 1.5 hours, or until the Bantha meat is very tender. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
  7. In a small bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour and cold water to create a slurry.
  8. Stir the slurry into the simmering stew. Add the Gribbet greens and cook for another 15-20 minutes, uncovered, or until the stew has thickened to your desired consistency and the greens are wilted.
  9. Taste and adjust seasonings as needed.
  10. Ladle the hot Bantha Stew into bowls and serve immediately.

Tips

  • For an even richer flavor, brown the Bantha meat a day ahead and refrigerate.
  • Serve with crusty bread or a side of roasted Wroshyr tree nuts for a complete Life Day meal.
  • This stew tastes even better the next day, allowing the flavors to meld further.
